.claude/hooks/constellation/agent-idle.s: This tells the project's tracking system that the AI assistant has gone quiet and is no longer actively working.
This tells the project's tracking system that the AI has picked up a new sub-task and started working on it.
.claude/hooks/constellation/agent-stop.s: This tells the project's tracking system that the AI has finished a sub-task.
.claude/hooks/constellation/agent-substo: This tells the project's tracking system that a background AI sub-task has ended.
Every time the AI uses a tool, this updates the tracking system with what the AI is doing right now.
.claude/hooks/constellation/description-: After a file is edited, this prompts the AI to update that file's plain-English description and record any new lessons learned about it.
.claude/hooks/constellation/learnings-su: Before a file is edited, this retrieves previously recorded lessons about that file and shows them to the AI so it can avoid repeating past mistakes.
.claude/hooks/constellation/lib/config.s: Wiring — connects other pieces together but doesn't really do anything on its own.
.claude/hooks/constellation/session-star: At the start of a new AI work session, this cleans up leftover tracking data from the previous session.
.claude/settings.json: Wiring — connects other pieces together but doesn't really do anything on its own.
.env.example: A template showing every secret key the site needs, with plain instructions on where to get or how to generate each one — fill it in to get the site running.
.gitignore: This is the list of files that the project's history machine should ignore — temporary files, secrets, and things too big to keep.
CLAUDE.md: Instructions written for AI coding assistants working on this project — covers GitHub hygiene rules, project overview, file layout, design conventions, and all the places visitors can send or receive data.
eslint.config.mjs: This is the rulebook for catching common coding mistakes automatically before they can ship to visitors.
next.config.ts: Wiring — connects other pieces together but doesn't really do anything on its own.
package.json: This is the project's name tag and shopping list — it says what this project is called and what other projects it relies on.
postcss.config.mjs: Wiring — connects other pieces together but doesn't really do anything on its own.
public/countries-110m.json: This is the geographic shape data for every country in the world, used to draw the conflict map.
README.md: Human-readable overview of the project for anyone who finds the repo online.
scripts/setup-supabase-blog-storage.sql: This is the one-time database setup that creates the image storage bucket for the blog.
scripts/setup-supabase-blog.sql: This is the one-time database setup that creates the blog posts table and all its rules about who can read or write what.
scripts/setup-supabase-conflict.sql: This is the one-time database setup that creates all the tables needed to run the Global Conflict Index.
src/app/api/ask-beau/route.ts: This is the brain of the AskBeau chatbot — it receives a visitor's question, calls the Gemini AI, streams back an answer, logs the conversation, and enforces hourly rate limits.
src/app/api/blog/admin/auth/route.ts: This checks whether the editor password is correct without ever revealing the password itself.
src/app/api/blog/categories/route.ts: This returns the list of blog categories — editors see all of them, while the public only sees categories attached to published posts.
src/app/api/blog/media/sign/route.ts: This generates a one-time secure address so the editor can upload an image directly to storage without routing the file through the site itself.
src/app/api/blog/posts/[slug]/route.ts: This reads, saves changes to, or permanently deletes a specific blog post identified by its URL slug.
src/app/api/blog/posts/route.ts: This lists all blog posts (or just the published ones for the public) and creates new blank drafts.
src/app/api/conflict/status/route.ts: This is a diagnostic check — it tells an authorized administrator exactly what conflict data the site has and when it was last updated, without exposing any secrets.
src/app/api/contact/route.ts: This receives a visitor's contact form submission, sanitizes it, and emails it straight to Beau's inbox.
src/app/api/global-conflict/news/route.t: This delivers the news headlines for a specific conflict, one page at a time, allowing the reader to load more as they scroll.
src/app/api/global-conflict/route.ts: This serves the full conflict map data — hotspots, global stats, and recent news — to the public-facing page.
src/app/api/pi-challenge/issue/route.ts: This generates a fresh challenge question (a code-sorting puzzle or a Star Trek quote) for the Pi easter egg.
This checks whether a visitor's answer to the Pi easter egg challenge is correct.
src/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx: This is the public page that displays a single published blog article by its URL.
src/app/blog/blog.css: This holds the colors, fonts, and animation details for the Terminal Notebook blog, kept separate so they don't spill into the rest of the site.
src/app/blog/edit/[slug]/page.tsx: This is the editor page for a specific blog post, gated behind the editor password.
src/app/blog/edit/new/page.tsx: This creates a new blank draft in the database and immediately sends the editor to it.
src/app/blog/edit/page.tsx: This is the editor's home screen showing all drafts and published posts in a grid.
src/app/blog/layout.tsx: This is the shared wrapper for every blog page — it sets the dark-purple Terminal Notebook theme, loads the reading font, and reads a saved cookie to remember the visitor's light-or-dark preference.
src/app/blog/page.tsx: This is the public blog index listing all published articles, with category filters and a search bar.
src/app/blog/preview/[slug]/page.tsx: This is a password-protected preview that lets the editor see exactly how a draft will look to readers before publishing.
src/app/global-conflict/page.tsx: This is the full Global Conflict Index page — it loads the latest data from the database and renders the world map, stat row, and news feed.
src/app/globals.css: This is the site's core visual recipe: background and surface colors, accent purple, text shades, animation keyframes, and a handful of utility styles.
src/app/layout.tsx: This is the outermost wrapper for the entire site — it sets the browser tab title, loads the display and mono fonts, and starts Google Analytics.
src/app/page.tsx: This is the main homepage that assembles every visible section in order: Header, Hero, metrics, case studies, BAD Labs, Modules, tools grid, career timeline, and footer.
src/components/AnalyticsProvider.tsx: This silently watches how visitors interact with the page — scrolling, clicking buttons, copying text — and sends those events to Google Analytics.
src/components/AskBeau.tsx: This is the chat box in the hero section where visitors type questions about Beau and receive AI-powered answers in real time.
src/components/BadLabsShowcase.tsx: This is the section of the homepage that highlights Beau's current venture, BAD Labs, including its three main offerings: Console CRM, custom AI tooling, and fractional leadership.
src/components/Blog/blocks/Blocks.tsx: This draws every type of content block a blog post can contain — headings, paragraphs, images, code snippets, tables, charts, video, audio, quotes, and more — plus the scrollable table of contents and the reading-progress bar at the top of the page.
src/components/Blog/Builder/AuthGate.tsx: This is the password prompt that guards the blog editor — it stores the password in the browser so you only have to enter it once per device.
src/components/Blog/Builder/blockKinds.t: This is the master catalog of all 20 block types the editor supports — each entry has a label, description, icon, and the default content it starts with.
src/components/Blog/Builder/CategoryDrop: This is the dropdown in the editor sidebar for picking an existing category or typing a new one for a blog post.
src/components/Blog/Builder/CommandPalet: This is the keyboard-shortcut overlay (⌘K) that lets the editor search and run commands without touching the mouse.
This is the tool in the editor sidebar for choosing a preset gradient cover or uploading a custom photo for a blog post.
src/components/Blog/Builder/DraftsList.t: This is the editor's home screen showing all drafts and published posts in a clickable grid.
src/components/Blog/Builder/editableBloc: These are the editable, in-place versions of every block type for use inside the editor, as opposed to the read-only versions that published readers see.
src/components/Blog/Builder/Editor.tsx: This is the main writing surface of the blog editor — it handles typing, block management, autosaving every 800 milliseconds, drag-and-drop reordering, and the publish flow.
src/components/Blog/Builder/EditorPage.t: This is the outer shell around the editor that handles password-checking and post-loading before handing off to the writing surface.
src/components/Blog/Builder/FloatingTool: This is the mini formatting bar — bold, italic, link, text color, size — that floats just above any text the editor has selected.
src/components/Blog/Builder/ImageUploadB: This is the upload button used throughout the editor to send image files directly to storage.
This creates a new blank draft in the database and immediately redirects the editor to it.
src/components/Blog/Builder/PublishModal: This is the dialog for publishing a post right now, scheduling it for a future date, or saving it back to draft.
src/components/Blog/Builder/Sidebar.tsx: This is the right-hand panel in the editor showing all post settings: URL slug, status, category, tags, cover, SEO description, and word-count stats.
src/components/Blog/Builder/SlashMenu.ts: This is the pop-up menu that appears when you type '/' in the editor, letting you insert any type of content block by name.
src/components/Blog/Builder/uploadHelper: This is the behind-the-scenes logic that sends an image from the editor to Supabase storage using a one-time signed upload address.
src/components/Blog/CoverBand.tsx: This is the decorative banner image at the top of a blog article — shared between the editor preview and the public reader so they always look identical.
src/components/Blog/Reader/ArticleView.t: This is the full layout for reading a single blog article: cover band, title, table of contents, body content, share links, and previous/next navigation.
src/components/Blog/Reader/IndexView.tsx: This is the public blog listing page with category chips for filtering and a title search bar.
src/components/Blog/Reader/PreviewArticl: This is the password-protected article preview that shows a draft exactly as it will look when published.
src/components/Blog/ThemeToggle.tsx: This is the button that switches the blog between dark and light mode and saves the visitor's preference for future visits.
src/components/Blog/Topbar.tsx: This is the macOS-style bar across the top of every blog page — it shows breadcrumb navigation, action buttons, and the light/dark toggle.
src/components/CaseStudies.tsx: This is the section of the homepage showing Beau's three major work stories — Expedia, Union, and BAD Labs — each expandable to reveal the full problem, what he built, and the results.
src/components/Footer.tsx: This is the contact form and social links at the bottom of the page.
src/components/GlitchText.tsx: This draws text that scrambles through random characters before snapping to the real word — used for dramatic effect in the Pi easter egg.
src/components/GlobalConflict/ConflictMa: This draws the interactive world map, tints each country by conflict intensity, and places pulsing red markers over every active hotspot.
src/components/GlobalConflict/ConflictTi: This is the news section below the map — it shows either the last 24 hours of global conflict headlines or the full archived timeline for whichever hotspot the visitor has selected.
src/components/GlobalConflict/global-con: This holds all the visual styling for the Global Conflict Index page, kept in its own file so it doesn't affect the rest of the site.
src/components/GlobalConflict/index.tsx: This is the full Global Conflict Index module — it assembles the stats row, the world map with tooltips and detail panels, and the news timeline into one cohesive page.
src/components/GlobalConflict/iso-countr: This is the lookup table that converts numeric country codes into readable country names for the map tooltips.
src/components/GlobalConflict/NewsFeed.t: This draws the list of individual news headlines in the conflict section, each one linking to the original article.
src/components/GlobalConflict/PageHeader: This is the top strip on the conflict page — it shows a back link, a live-data status badge, and how recently the conflict data was updated.
This draws the small bar chart in the conflict detail panel that gives a quick visual sense of trend for the selected conflict.
src/components/GlobalConflict/StatCard.t: This draws one animated number card in the conflict stats row — for example, 'Active armed conflicts: 34' — with a count-up animation when the page loads.
src/components/GoogleAnalytics.tsx: This loads the Google Analytics tracking script and fires a page-view event every time the visitor navigates to a new page.
src/components/Header.tsx: This is the fixed navigation bar pinned to the top of every page — it shows Beau's name, his positioning line, and his current availability status.
src/components/Hero.tsx: This is the first thing visitors see: Beau's name, title trifecta, headline, career proof statement, the two call-to-action buttons, his headshot, and the AskBeau chat box.
src/components/Modules/index.tsx: This is the 'Modules' section of the homepage — it shows two cards, one for the Global Conflict Index and one for the blog, each with live data pulled from the database.
src/components/Modules/ModuleCard.tsx: This draws a single clickable card in the Modules section, linking to one of Beau's live projects and showing its real-time stats (post count, last updated, etc.).
src/components/PiEasterEgg/ClassifiedLog: This draws the fake 'classified government access' login screen that accepts any credentials after three failed attempts, part of the Pi easter egg sequence.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/Dashboard.tsx: This is the final screen of the Pi easter egg: a terminal-style dashboard showing the current time and a link to the blog editor.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/GlitchTransit: This plays the brief visual glitch effect — static noise, screen tears, color shifts — that transitions between screens in the Pi easter egg.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/HackingSequen: This is the animated montage of fake government login screens (Stanford, Lockheed, CIA, NSA, etc.) that plays after a visitor clicks the hidden π symbol.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/index.tsx: This orchestrates the entire Pi easter egg from start to finish — idle π → hacking sequence → classified login → terminal challenge → dashboard.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/PiSymbol.tsx: This is the nearly invisible π that appears in a random corner of the footer after a delay — clicking it kicks off the entire easter egg.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/screens/AWSCo: This draws a fake AWS Management Console login screen that auto-types credentials and grants access as part of the hacking sequence.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/screens/CIALo: This draws a fake CIA classified network login screen for the hacking sequence.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/screens/index: Wiring — connects other pieces together but doesn't really do anything on its own.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/screens/Lockh: This draws a fake Lockheed Martin employee portal login screen for the hacking sequence.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/screens/MI6Lo: This draws a fake MI6 / SIS secure portal login screen for the hacking sequence.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/screens/NSALo: This draws a fake NSA terminal login screen styled as pure text output for the hacking sequence.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/screens/Penta: This draws a fake Pentagon SIPRNET access portal login screen for the hacking sequence.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/screens/Stanf: This draws a fake Stanford University WebLogin screen, the first stop in the hacking sequence.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/screens/Unkno: This draws the climax of the hacking sequence: a mystery database with glitching red text and a fake firewall bypass animation.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/TerminalLogin: This is the real authentication challenge in the easter egg: a code-sorting puzzle followed by a Star Trek quote completion test.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/types.ts: This is the agreed-upon list of named shapes that all the Pi easter egg pieces use when passing information between each other.
src/components/PiEasterEgg/useAutoType.t: This makes text appear to type itself one character at a time — used by every fake login screen in the easter egg.
src/components/SystemKernel.tsx: This draws the 'Tools & Platforms' grid on the homepage, listing every tool Beau uses across four categories: AI & Automation, Platforms & CRMs, Development, and Operations.
src/components/TelemetryGrid.tsx: This draws the 'By the Numbers' section — eight key career metrics displayed in a 4×2 grid, each counting up from zero when they scroll into view.
src/components/TerminalAnimation.tsx: This draws an animated terminal window that types out fake command outputs highlighting Beau's career impact — it exists but is not currently shown on the main page.
src/components/Timeline.tsx: This is the collapsible full career history section at the bottom of the homepage, listing every role Beau has held in reverse chronological order.
src/components/ui/Button.tsx: This is a reusable button that comes in two styles: a solid purple primary and a transparent outlined secondary.
src/components/ui/EnergyButton.tsx: This is the large rounded button used for the main calls-to-action in the hero section.
src/components/ui/Skeleton.tsx: This draws animated placeholder shapes that pulse grey while content is still loading.
src/hooks/useTrackSection.ts: This watches whether a section of the page has scrolled into the visitor's view, and fires a Google Analytics event the moment it does.
src/lib/analytics.ts: This is the organized list of every Google Analytics event the site can fire — contact form steps, chatbot interactions, easter egg milestones, scroll depth, and more.
src/lib/blog-auth.ts: This checks whether an incoming request carries the correct editor password before allowing any write operation.
src/lib/blog-data.ts: These are the public-facing entry points for reading blog posts — they return empty results gracefully if the database isn't connected.
src/lib/blog-media.ts: This generates one-time secure upload addresses for blog images, validating file type and size before issuing the address.
src/lib/blog-store.ts: This handles all the database reads and writes for the blog: fetching posts, creating drafts, saving edits, and deleting posts.
src/lib/blog-utils.ts: This is a collection of small tools for the blog: counting words, calculating read time, extracting headings for the table of contents, generating URL-safe slugs, and cleaning up category names.
src/lib/chat-log.ts: This saves every AskBeau conversation to the database, with the visitor's IP address anonymized for privacy.
src/lib/conflict-data.ts: This defines the shapes of all conflict data objects and provides the main entry point for fetching the current conflict map data from whichever source is available.
src/lib/conflict-store.ts: This handles all the database reads for the conflict map — latest global snapshot, active hotspots, recent news headlines, and the list of countries involved in each conflict.
src/lib/cron-auth.ts: This checks whether an incoming request carries the correct administrative secret key before allowing access to protected diagnostic endpoints.
src/lib/data.ts: This is the single source of truth for every piece of content on the portfolio: career metrics, full job history, skills, case studies, hero text, social links, and the module descriptions on the homepage.
src/lib/module-telemetry.ts: This fetches the live counts and timestamps shown on the homepage module cards — how many conflicts are active, how many posts are published, and when each was last updated.
src/lib/pi-challenge/server.ts: This holds all the Star Trek quotes and code-sorting puzzles used in the Pi easter egg challenge, plus the logic for picking a random one and checking whether the visitor's answer is correct.
src/lib/pi-challenge/token.ts: This creates and verifies tamper-proof challenge tokens using a cryptographic signature, so a visitor can't skip the Pi challenge by faking a 'correct answer' claim.
src/lib/rate-limit.ts: This enforces per-visitor hourly limits on chatbot questions and contact form submissions, using the database to track counts.
src/lib/supabase.ts: This creates the database connection, trying three different sets of environment variable names in priority order until it finds one that works.
src/proxy.ts: This is the security layer that attaches protective headers — including a strict Content Security Policy — to every page response before it reaches the visitor's browser.
src/types/index.ts: This is the single file that defines every named data shape the project uses: metrics, job history, blog posts, conflict data, chatbot messages, contact forms, and more.
